assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clean, unambiguous discovery from nature: the last unknown neutrino mixing angle turned out to be surprisingly large, which opens the door to leptonic CP-violation searches and shapes the whole future neutrino programme. The discovery comes first here, and it is exactly the kind of clue from experiment that I value.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) and RENO (Kim) made the decisive reactor measurements; I recall that Double Chooz and the T2K appearance result also contributed, and the credited trio is a plausible, fair configuration, though the Double Chooz leadership is not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by several reactor experiments within months and consistently refined for over a decade; the interpretation within three-flavour oscillations is stable. Timely.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit means leadership rather than sole authorship is being honoured; the exact roles of individuals are from my memory, not independently verified.
Overlap with earlier neutrino-oscillation recognition (2015) may make the committee ask whether this is a sufficiently distinct discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A conceptual and experimental landmark: the Z2 topological insulator and quantum spin Hall effect introduced a new classification of phases tied to band topology, with a rapid experimental realization. It has reshaped condensed matter physics and links to materials and quantum devices.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction and Z2 classification; Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The BHZ theorists are not in the credited names, so credit allocation is an unresolved question.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of independent confirmation in HgTe, Bi-based materials and ARPES; the interpretation is stable and widely used. Recognition is timely, bordering on overdue given the 2016 prize covered the earlier topological phase work.
uncertainties: Whether the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions makes this feel like partial duplication.
Credit to Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and to experimental ARPES groups is not captured by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos opened a new window on the extreme universe and is a true discovery with an existential flavour, answering where the highest-energy cosmic particles come from. Later source associations (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, the Galactic plane) strengthened the case.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the single credited person as the driving force behind IceCube; a one-person prize for a large collaboration instrument is possible but leaves out others who built and analysed the detector, and I cannot verify from the supplied data who else would be required.
assessment.maturity: Observation confirmed with growing significance by IceCube and corroborated by independent analyses; source identification is still evolving but the existence of the flux is secure.
uncertainties: Single-name credit for a large collaboration raises fairness questions.
The astrophysical origin of most of the flux remains open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP turned cosmology into a precision science, fixing the age, composition and geometry of the universe with the first full-sky high-resolution CMB maps and providing the strongest early evidence for the concordance cosmology of dark matter and dark energy. This is directly relevant to the matters I try to explain with coffee cups.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page designed and calibrated the instrument and Spergel led the cosmological interpretation. A three-person prize looks coherent, although the CMB field has already been recognised (COBE 2006, cosmology 2019).
assessment.maturity: Fully corroborated by Planck and by ground and balloon experiments; very mature, perhaps late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior CMB and cosmology prizes could be judged as already covered.
Roles of other WMAP team members, e.g. Wollack or Hinshaw, are not captured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle followed by the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene: theory guided by nature and then confirmed by experiment. It created the whole field of moire quantum materials.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the quantitative prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group discovered the correlated states and superconductivity. Cao et al. and other experimentalists, as well as Kim, Dean and Young, also made major contributions, so the allocation is partly unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups worldwide within a few years; the mechanism of superconductivity is not yet settled, which suggests the prize might be timely for the discovery but not for the full interpretation.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved.
Other contributors such as Yuan Cao or the earlier Lopes dos Santos et al. work may deserve credit; I have not verified this.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution connects fundamental quantum mechanics (no-cloning, entanglement, Bell tests) to a practical technology; BB84 and Ekert's E91 are original, clear and have become the basis of a global research and industrial field.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are clearly decisive through BB84; Ekert's independent entanglement-based protocol is also a distinct and original contribution. The three-person configuration fits well, though Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is a historical complication that is not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally demonstrated over fiber and satellite links; security proofs are mature, but practical deployment and side-channel issues remain. Recognition would be timely given the 2022 Bell-test prize.
uncertainties: Wiesner's earlier unpublished work and his death complicate credit.
Impact as physics versus engineering technology could be debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations provide a standard ruler anchored in early-universe physics and are now a central probe of dark energy; the discovery in galaxy surveys fits my interest in clues from nature about the nature of cosmic acceleration.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein (SDSS) and Cole (2dFGRS) detected the peak in galaxy clustering in 2005; the theoretical prediction traces to Sunyaev and Zeldovich and Peebles and Yu, so credit among Peebles (already a laureate), Sunyaev and others is complicated. Percival is plausible as a fourth option but I limit myself to three.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many surveys, including BOSS and DESI; a cornerstone of the standard cosmology. Mature, though the cosmology field was recognised in 2011 and 2019.
uncertainties: Complicated allocation with a theoretical lineage that includes an existing laureate.
Current DESI hints for evolving dark energy may be a tension rather than a confirmation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, from Katori's magic-wavelength proposal to Ye's record-setting realisations, give the most precise measurements ever made and test fundamental constants, relativistic time dilation at the millimetre scale and possible dark-matter couplings.
assessment.attribution: Katori invented the concept and Ye achieved key ultra-stable demonstrations; the two-person configuration is clean, though Hall, Hansch (2005) and ion-clock groups such as those of Wineland and Hollberg have already been recognised earlier.
assessment.maturity: Independently realised by many labs and compared across continents; redefinition of the second is under discussion, so the timing is plausible but not urgent.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the 2005 and 2012 precision-measurement prizes.
Contributions of Lemonde, Takamoto and others are not covered by the supplied names.
